attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses the claim in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the categorical present-tense claims and omits the explicitly subjective commentary. No stated condition or deadline is lost.

contract.note: Including bounded autonomous task completion is a fair ordinary reading of the categorical denial of any proof. Tool-equipped agents are relevant in this context, provided bounded success is distinguished from dependable general autonomy, as the contract requires.

evidence.note: The version-pinned March 2025 evaluation demonstrates bounded autonomous completion, contradicting the denial of any proof. Its roughly 50% success threshold does not establish dependable general autonomy or independent replication.

The contemporaneous evaluation documents consequential execution, planning and recovery failures, supporting the concern about dependable autonomous work. It does not establish an absolute inability to operate autonomously.

reviews.rationale: Bounded autonomous task completion had been demonstrated before publication, undermining the categorical denial of proof. Repeated execution and recovery failures support the narrower reliability concern. Neither study establishes broad dependable autonomy or proves that LLMs categorically cannot deliver consistency, reliability and replicability.
